chapter: Cafe Society and the Zodiac Suite
title: Cafe Society: Josh White, Barney Josephson and Johnny Garrett
summary: At Cafe Society she worked solo. Johnny Garrett, the valet, made her smile with a Bronx cheer; Josh White and Imogene Coca are among those she remembers.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: There you had a group, right?

I did solo. I worked with - Edmond Hall's group was there and they later moved to the Cafe uptown. They had various groups while I was there - Josh White. It was such a beautiful thing to work in the Cafe. I remember times when one act wasn't going well, Josh White and Johnny Garrett would come out and boost us. I never smiled when I was playing and Barney Josephson, the owner of the club, did everything he could to try to get me to smile. He came down, he had me acting like Hazel and all that. Eddie Hayward said, "Leave her alone. She'll get to it."

So one night I was playing and Johnny Garrett used to walk in back of me to make me smile. He'd do the Bronx cheer and I'd laugh. Barney happened to be there and he said, "What do you mean doing that and that's my star act." Johnny said, "You wanted her to smile, didn't you? Look at her now." And so he gave Johnny a raise.

Johnny Garrett came to the Cafe as a valet for us, where he pushed the piano on and off. He learned a great deal while he was there and he went out with Sarah and helped make her Vaughan/great. He's a terrific man. He just watched and he learned through watching and he became a great manager. Through him and Sarah Vaughan's husband and the pianist, they really brought her out in good style to the public.
You know Johnny's the maitre de at a restaurant around here now? Rust Brown?

Yes, he's terrific. He knows the lighting and he knows everything. Imogene Coca was with us there and she was the type that was always nervous about going on. She walked through the club and when she got to the ladies' dressing room - we all dressed in the same room - she'd say, "Oh, we're not going to go over. I know it; I can feel it." And Johnny would hype her real good, make her do a real good show. He was very good at that.
